newsitem.title: UK: Ashtead sees 1st rise in UK demand since '90.
newsitem.headline: Ashtead sees 1st rise in UK demand since '90.

text.p: British plant machinery hire firm Ashtead Group Plc said on Monday that trading had started well in the new year and signs of an increase in UK demand held out the "promise of a recovery in hire rates".
"The current year has begun well and for the first time since 1990 we anticipate an increase in demand in the UK," chairman Peter Lewis said in the results statement.
"In both the UK and U.S., there is an inexorable move towards the outsourcing of plant requirements which will be to Ashtead's competitive advantage," he added.

Earlier, the group reported a 68 percent increase in pre-tax profits to 28.3 million stg for the year to April 30, as well as a 20 percent jump in the total dividend to 3.65 pence per share. Turnover rose 54 percent to 147.5 million stg.
"These are very good results in a year in which conditions in the UK were particularly competitive," Lewis said.
"We expect to benefit from growth in all our markets, which will be enhanced by the inevitable rationalisation of our industries in the UK and U.S."

Ashtead is market leader for plant hire in the UK -- at 14 percent of the market compared with four percent five years ago -- with its A-Plant division and one of the top 10 operators in the United States with Sunbelt.

It expects to continue to grow both organically and by acquisition. This year it expects to open 30 more of its Profit Centres in the UK and the United States. It opened 18 last year, taking it to 148 in the UK and 30 in the United States.
The group's third division -- Ashtead Technology -- has centres in Aberdeen, Singapore and Houston, and expects to benefit from the strength of the world oil and gas industries.
Shares in Ashtead were up 9.0 pence at 301-1/2 at 0835 GMT.
